modified_caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.

modifications.reality: GPT-4o actually peaks at 34.4% accuracy at a tree width of 5, not 31.1%.

modifications.claim: Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforms GPT-4o across all tree widths.
modifications.reality: Claude-3.5-Sonnet does not consistently outperform GPT-4o; GPT-4o has higher accuracy at tree widths of 3, 5, and 7.

modifications.claim: The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits an inverted U-shaped trend for both models.
modifications.reality: While GPT-4o does exhibit an inverted U-shaped trend, Claude-3.5-Sonnet does not; its accuracy decreases after the initial increase at tree width 3.

correct_elements: Chart type is a line plot.
X-axis is labeled 'Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)' and spans from 1 to 7.
Y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy@1 (%)' and spans from 15% to 35%.
The legend correctly identifies the two models as 'GPT-4o' and 'Claude-3.5-Sonnet'.
The general observation that GPT-4o peaks at a higher accuracy than Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
